name: Understanding what's in images and video
gist: Teaching models to recognize, locate, and segment objects in visual data—what things are, where they are, and their boundaries.
explain: This is the core of computer vision: teaching machines to recognize objects and understand scenes. The basic task is simple in principle but hard in practice: given a photo, identify what objects are in it, where they are located, and trace their exact boundaries. A cat sitting on a chair is three problems stacked together. First, detect the cat — find a box around it. Second, classify it — label that box 'cat.' Third, segment it — outline every pixel that belongs to the cat, pixel by pixel, so you know where the cat ends and the chair begins.

The challenge is that the same object looks completely different depending on viewpoint, lighting, scale, and occlusion. A cat's face from the front versus from the side are almost different creatures. Shadows make edges vanish. A tiny cat far away might have fewer pixels than a close-up whisker. Other objects hide parts of the scene. Real-world photos are messier than textbook examples: extreme angles, partial views, clutter. The model must learn to recognize the concept 'cat' despite all this variation. And it must do this not just for cats, but for hundreds or thousands of object classes in a single image.

Papers in this subtheme use deep neural networks trained on large labeled datasets to learn what features matter. Some focus on detecting boxes around objects as fast as possible, trading precision for speed. Others refine the boxes and add pixel-level segmentation masks. Some use two-stage pipelines: first find regions of interest, then classify and refine them. Others use single-stage detectors that predict everything at once. A few split the image into small tiles and learn which tiles relate to the same object by computing relationships between all pairs of tiles. The aim is always the same: extract precise, useful information about what is in the scene and where.

papers.title: SLIP-RS: Structured-Attribute Language-Image Pre-Training for Remote Sensing Object Detection
papers.contribution: Extensive experiments demonstrate that SLIP-RS establishes unprecedented performance in fine-grained detection and cross-domain generalization, validating structured attributes as a vital foundation for scalable remote sensing models

papers.title: SONAR: Spectral‑Contrastive Audio Residuals for Generalizable Deepfake Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on ASVspoof 2021 in a single-run setting while converging faster than strong baselines.

papers.title: Salient Object Ranking via Cyclical Perception-Viewing Interaction Modeling
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on SOR benchmarks by modeling explicit top-down cognitive pathways through cyclical perception-viewing interaction.

papers.title: Seg-ReSearch: Segmentation with Interleaved Reasoning and External Search
papers.contribution: Substantially improves state-of-the-art on OK-VOS benchmark and existing reasoning segmentation tasks by enabling external knowledge integration for open-world segmentation.

papers.title: Segment Any Events with Language
papers.contribution: Outperformed proposed baselines in performance and inference speed with parameter-efficient architecture and curated benchmarks across granularity levels.

papers.title: Segment Anything with Robust Uncertainty-Accuracy Correlation
papers.contribution: Improves segmentation quality and yields faithful uncertainty with stronger correlation across 23 zero-shot domains.

papers.title: Self-Guided Low Light Object Detection Framework
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on low-light benchmarks with no additional inference cost and outperforms domain adaptation methods.

papers.title: Sequential Information Bottleneck Fusion: Towards Robust and Generalizable Multi-Modal Brain Tumor Segmentation
papers.contribution: SMSN consistently outperforms parallel fusion baselines on BRATS18/20 with robustness in missing-modality settings and superior cross-domain generalization to brain metastasis datasets.

papers.title: SpaCeFormer: Fast Proposal-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Segmentation
papers.contribution: 0.12–0.30 seconds per scene (2–3 orders of magnitude faster); 21× higher mask recall than prior methods; 11.1 zero-shot mAP on ScanNet200.

papers.title: SpaceVista: All-Scale Visual Spatial Reasoning from mm to km
papers.contribution: SpaceVista-7B demonstrates competitive performance across 5 benchmarks, showcasing generalization across all scales and diverse scenarios.

papers.title: Supervise Less, See More: Training-free Nuclear Instance Segmentation with Prototype-Guided Prompting
papers.contribution: SPROUT achieves competitive nuclear instance segmentation performance without supervision or retraining across multiple histopathology benchmarks.

papers.title: Symbiosis-Inspired Knowledge Distillation for Incremental Object Detection
papers.contribution: Preserve old class knowledge and stabilize semantic topology during incremental learning over existing class-incremental methods.

papers.title: T-measure: A Topology-Consistent Metric for Binary Segmentation
papers.contribution: Performs exceptionally in downstream tasks with high consistency with human visual perception across diverse complex scenarios.

papers.title: Temporal-Emerged Prompting for Segment Anything in Multiframe Infrared Small Target Detection
papers.contribution: TEP-SAM effectively adapts SAM to multiframe infrared small target detection, particularly under severely low-SNR conditions.

papers.title: Towards Effective Waste Segmentation for Automated Waste Recycling in Cluttered Background
papers.contribution: Extensive experimentation on ZeroWaste-aug, ZeroWaste-f and SpectralWaste datasets reveals merits of the method in cluttered waste detection scenarios.

papers.title: Towards Reliable Detection of Empty Space: Conditional Marked Point Processes for Object Detection
papers.contribution: Introduces a spatial statistics framework that provides well-defined confidence estimates for empty regions, demonstrated through calibration assessments.

papers.title: UGround: Towards Unified Visual Grounding with Unrolled Transformers
papers.contribution: Unifies visual grounding across attribute perspectives (from refer expression segmentation to new tasks) while reducing cumulative errors through dynamic layer selection and explicit spatial guidance.

papers.title: Unleashing the Representational Power of Fourier Shapes for Attacking Infrared Object Detection
papers.contribution: Physical patches achieve over 88% attack success rate at distances greater than 25m, demonstrating striking robustness across diverse distances, angles, poses, and individuals.

papers.title: Unsupervised Camouflaged Object Detection with Dual-Eigenvector Spectral Pseudo-Labeling and Contrastive Refinement
papers.contribution: Outperforms existing UCOD methods by generating high-quality pseudo-labels and explicitly incorporating boundary information.

papers.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning for 3D Mesh Parameterization with Semantic and Visibility Objectives
papers.contribution: The method produces UV atlases supporting better texture generation and reducing perceptible seam artifacts compared to recent state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: VIP: Visual-guided Prompt Evolution for Efficient Dense Vision-Language Inference
papers.contribution: Surpasses top methods by 1.4-8.4% mIoU, generalizes to diverse domains, requires marginal inference overhead.

papers.title: VSCD: Video-based Scene Change Detection in Unaligned Scenes
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on a large-scale 1.1M-frame benchmark and demonstrates real-world impact on a mobile robot for visual surveillance and incremental learning.

papers.title: Veritas: Generalizable Deepfake Detection via Pattern-Aware Reasoning
papers.contribution: Achieves significant gains across out-of-domain scenarios (unseen forgeries, data domains, model architectures) with transparent, faithful detection outputs.

papers.title: VidGuard-R1: AI-Generated Video Detection and Explanation via Reasoning MLLMs and RL
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on benchmarks, exceeding 95% accuracy with training, delivering precise and interpretable detection rationales.

papers.title: Video Scene Segmentation with Genre and Duration Signals
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on MovieNet-SSeg and BBC datasets with an extended MovieChat-SSeg benchmark covering movies, TV series, and documentaries.

papers.title: VideoVeritas: AI-Generated Video Detection via Perception Pretext Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves balanced performance across diverse benchmarks with a new MintVid dataset of 3K videos from nine generators plus factual-error annotations.

papers.title: VisionReasoner: Unified Reasoning-Integrated Visual Perception via Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: VisionReasoner achieves 29.1% relative improvement on COCO detection, 22.1% on ReasonSeg segmentation, and 13.2% on CountBench counting compared to Qwen2.5VL baseline.

papers.title: WIMFRIS: WIndow Mamba Fusion and Parameter Efficient Tuning for Referring Image Segmentation
papers.contribution: WIMFRIS achieves new state-of-the-art performance across all public RIS benchmarks.

papers.title: WavePolyp: Video Polyp Segmentation via Hierarchical Wavelet-Based Feature Aggregation and Inter-Frame Divergence Perception
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods on SUN-SEG and CVC-612 datasets with improved real-time performance.

papers.title: Weakly Supervised Cross-Modal Learning for 4D Radar Scene Flow Estimation
papers.contribution: Surpasses state-of-the-art cross-modal supervised approaches and fully supervised scene flow methods on the View-of-Delft dataset without requiring 3D multi-object tracking on dense LiDAR.

papers.title: You Point, I Learn: Online Adaptation of Interactive Segmentation Models for Handling Distribution Shifts in Medical Imaging
papers.contribution: The approach consistently outperforms baselines on 5 fundus and 4 brain-MRI databases by leveraging user corrections as pseudo-ground-truth for online adaptation.

papers.title: Zero-shot HOI Detection with MLLM-based Detector-agnostic Interaction Recognition
papers.contribution: Achieves superior zero-shot performance with strong cross-dataset generalization and flexibility to integrate with any object detectors without retraining.
